newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - PIHP becomes big conglomerate overnight.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - PIHP becomes big conglomerate overnight.

text.p: Pernas International Holdings Bhd has become a major Malaysian conglomerate after acquiring the assets of state investment firm Perbadanan Nasional last week, company officials said on Monday.

PIHP is getting eight hotels, two more office buildings, and 194,000 acres (78,000 hectares) of oil palm plantation from the privatisation of Perbadanan Nasional, which the government set up in 1969 as a vehicle to help ethnic Malays get started in business.
The company takes over a land bank of 4,300 acres (1,740 hectares), an engineering and construction firm and Pernas assets in other Southeast Asian countries.

It also inherits Pernas's controlling stakes in three listed companies: Tradewinds (M) Bhd, involved in plantations, sugar refining and insurance; Malayawata Steel Bhd; and United Malayan Land Bhd, which is building a 5.5 billion ringgit ($2.2 billion) township in southern Johor state.
"PIHB will be one of the largest groups in Malaysia," company chairman Shahriman Tunku Sulaiman told a briefing on Monday for analysts and journalists on last week's privatisation.
Shahriman and 13 other managers of the company took a controlling 32 percent stake in the enlarged PIHP in the biggest management buyout in Malaysia's history.
Shahriman said his group paid 495 million ringgit for the stake, financed by a loan from a local financial institution on very favourable terms. He declined to give details.

Deputy General Manager Mohamed Khadar Merican said the acquisitions transform PIHB into a major conglomerate eligible to be included in the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Composite Index of the 100 biggest companies.

Shahriman said PIHB aims to hit the half-billion ringgit mark in net profit in five years. That is an ambitious undertaking, given that the company is projecting net profit (after minorities) of 51.4 million ringgit in fiscal year 1997 (ending January 31) and 42.41 million in 1996.
Turnover was 1.16 billion ringgit in 1996 against 1.07 billion the year before.

PIHB is paying 1.146 billion ringgit for the new assets. Some 600 million ringgit of the purchase price will be financed by issuing 250 million new shares at 2.40 ringgit each, another 280 million will be raised through a bond issue with warrants and the rest will come from internal funds, Mohamed said.

PIHP, formerly known as Pernas International Hotels and Properties, was transformed overnight into Malaysia's biggest hotel operator when it acquired eight in the privatisation. It had three hotels previously and plans to build two more.
The privatisation gives PIHB a total of five office buildings, whose total book cost is 1.06 billion ringgit.

It gives PIHB stakes in two residential property projects -- the 1,000-acre (400 hectare) Bangi Heights south of Kuala Lumpur valued at 1.2 billion ringgit and the 3,300-acre (1,335 hectare) Seri Alam township in Johor, across the straits from Singapore, valued at 5.5 billion ringgit.
PIHB has suddenly become a major force in the oil palm sector with 194,000 acres (78,000 acres) currently and plans to expand to 300,000 acres over the next five years.
Shahriman said PIHP had plans as well for refining and marketing palm oil, of which Malaysia is the largest producer and exporter.

He said the company was in the final stages of negotiations with a cosmetics firm to sell palm oil as a base for cosmetics. Asked if that company was Avon Products, Inc he said: "That's a very good guess".
